messages.content: When does heat season start in NYC?

upstream.answer: Heat season in NYC runs October 1 through May 31. Between 6 AM and 10 PM, if it is below 55°F outside, the inside must be at least 68°F. Between 10 PM and 6 AM, the inside must be at least 62°F at all times, whatever the outside temperature. Hot water must be at least 120°F all year. That is NYC311's published summary (KA-01036), not legal advice; Housing Court Answers (212-962-4795) can tell you how it applies to you.

citations_include: NY Real Property Law § 235-b · NYC311, Residential Heat and Hot Water Requirements (KA-01036)

messages.content: There's no heat in my apartment. What should I do?

upstream.answer: Here is what the published guidance says. From October 1 through May 31, the inside must be at least 62°F between 10 PM and 6 AM at all times, and at least 68°F between 6 AM and 10 PM whenever it is below 55°F outside (NYC311, KA-01036). NY Real Property Law § 235-b also makes every residential lease carry a warranty that the premises are fit for human habitation. This building already has 1 open class-C violation on record. Worth documenting: the dates and times the heat was out, indoor temperatures photographed with a timestamp, and every 311 complaint number. HPD investigates maintenance complaints filed through 311, and NYC311 says that if the problem isn't fixed you can take legal action in Housing Court. I can't tell you what to do in your situation, but Housing Court Answers (212-962-4795) and the Met Council Tenants Rights Hotline (212-979-0611) can.
